finalText:
All 40 cases pass now.

**Root cause:** `computeTotal` rounded to USD cents after each discount step, before currency conversion. That's rounding twice — once mid-calculation, once at the end — which real financial rounding shouldn't do. Percent coupons (unlike flat ones) produce extra decimal digits (e.g. $19.98 × 0.9 = $17.982), and truncating that to $17.98 before multiplying by a non-USD rate could push the final result across a cent boundary. Fixed by carrying full precision through both discount steps and rounding only once, after conversion.
